learning: First-iteration baseline. Race telemetry from this package will show whether the 6 cm span saturates on sharp bends, whether kd lag causes oscillation at base_speed 1.2, and whether slalom line loss dominates completion time.
notes: Baseline package: Builder geometry unchanged, symmetric five-sensor weights scaled to ±1, moderate kp/kd, base_speed 1.2, last_direction line-loss recovery. Based on no race data yet; the expected outcome is a hypothesis to test.
rationale: This is the first iteration, so there is no race telemetry yet. I keep the Builder's baseline geometry unchanged so that the controller is tested on the platform as proposed. Sensor x-positions run from -0.03 (right) to +0.03 (left). Weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1] follow the same sign convention, so a line under the left sensors gives a positive signal, which steers left. The sum of weights at full coverage stays within ±1, which keeps signal scale moderate. Sensor y = 0.05 m gives roughly 0.05 m of lead, which should let the controller see the line before the wheels reach it. With the 0.12 m track and 0.03 m wheels, a turn command of about 1 unit gives roughly 700 PWM of wheel difference out of 4095, so kp = 2.5 is a moderate authority. kd = 0.4 damps the response without much phase lag at base_speed 1.2. ki = 0.05 is small, to avoid windup on the long bends. base_speed 1.2 gives an average speed that should finish the roughly 4.5 m course in under 3 s, while staying below full PWM to leave headroom for turns. line_loss = last_direction re-enters the line on the side it left, which suits the slalom. Expected result: a completed run on oval and s-bend, with the slalom the most likely source of line loss. This expectation is a hypothesis, not a measured result.
